summary: Sharp rise in 5xx for long-lived streaming sessions after client SDK hedged-retry rollout
description:
Issue summary:
We observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses for long-lived streaming endpoints beginning ~2026-03-14T01:10Z on the us-east production fleet serving dedicated customers. Errors are concentrated on streaming routes ("/v1/chat/stream") and manifest as rapid connection rejects (502/503) and occasional 500s from the serving-runtime process prior to connection teardown.

Impact:
- Customer Acme Analytics reported elevated error rates (~18% of streaming sessions failing) and multiple downstream user-facing timeouts in their production integration.
- Latency for successful streams increased by ~120ms p50 and p95 latency rose substantially.
- A few runtimes show worker exits (OOM-like symptoms) correlated with the same timeframe.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east), Dedicated tenant pool for Acme Analytics, tagged cluster: ded-cluster-17
- Affected models: redwood-open-v2-7b (primary), fallback open-chat-7b
- Client side: Acme updated SDK to redwood-js v2.3.1 at ~2026-03-14T00:55Z (they confirmed rollout to a small percentage of hosts internally).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start a long-lived streaming session with a large initial context (>8k tokens).
2) Observe initial prefix prefetch / KV warmup activity from runtime (spikes in NVMe I/O).
3) Client-side hedged-retry (new default in SDK v2.3.1) issues aggressive parallel requests on perceived slow first-byte from the gateway.
4) Load balancer closes one of the half-open sockets (ALPN/TLS subtle downgrade observed), triggering client to reissue requests and the gateway to enqueue more accept connections.
5) Accept queue and ephemeral worker pool grow; runtime performs additional prefetches causing KV eviction thrash and occasional worker OOM / process restarts.
6) Elevated 5xx and streaming disconnects are reported.

Observed behavior:
- Grafana: spike in apigw 5xx rate at 2026-03-14T01:10Z (from baseline <0.2% to 8% over 10 minutes).
- Datadog: serving-runtime process in affected nodes shows memory growth followed by restart traces, NVMe iowait spike, and increased prefetch queue length.
- Access logs: multiple concurrent requests with identical payloads (hedged retries) from same client IP ranges.

Expected behavior:
- Long-lived streams should be stable; hedged retries should not cascade into resource thrash or trigger runtime restarts.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- At 2026-03-14T02:00Z support applied a temporary ingress circuit-breaker for Acme's tenant pool limiting concurrent hedged attempts to 1 (effectively disabling parallel hedged retries at apigw level). This reduced 5xx to ~1.1% in the next 25 minutes.
- Notified Acme to pause their internal SDK rollout to the rest of their fleet (they acknowledged at 2026-03-14T02:12Z).

Next steps / proposed remediation:
- Short term: roll apigw rate limiting rule to other dedicated clusters to throttle parallel hedged attempts for streaming routes until a safer retry policy is deployed.
- Medium term: add accept-queue backpressure signals from runtime to gateway to avoid creating excess ephemeral workers when prefetch backlog is high.
- Long term: update SDK guidance and release a server-side header to inform clients of server-side perceived first-byte latency to avoid aggressive retries.

References / links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/apigw/streaming-5xx?from=now-1h&to=now (internal)
- Datadog process traces: https://app.datadoghq.com/processes?runtimes=ded-cluster-17
- Slack thread: #support (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C04SUPPORT/p1626234000000)
- Confluence runbook (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/streaming-hedged-retry-incident-handling

investigation_notes: Correlation between SDK v2.3.1 hedged-retry default and 5xx spike confirmed via request fingerprints and user-agent strings.
Accept-queue depth increased 6x during the spike; we observed ~2x ephemeral worker spin-up rate compared to baseline.
Runtime logs show repeated prefetch requests for the same prefix across concurrent workers leading to KV cache invalidation and increased memory pressure.

Hypothesis: aggressive hedged retry + transient TLS/ALPN handshake flakiness at load balancer causes duplicate inflight work that the runtime cannot coordinate, leading to resource thrash and occasional process exits.
Reproduced locally in staging by running synthetic hedged-retry client against a long-prefetch model; saw accept queue growth and sustained I/O.

[2026-03-14T01:11:12Z] runtime: nvme_iowait=78% node=ded-node-17-03 prefetch_queue=84 mem_rss=12.3GB pid=4421
resolution_notes: Temporary apigw rule (rl-8332) applied to throttle parallel hedged attempts for streaming routes in Acme tenant pool. Customer paused SDK rollout. Engineering to implement a server-side backpressure signal and coordinate with SDK team to change the default hedged-retry policy for streaming routes. Follow-up action: create a short-term deploy to add a server header (X-Server-FirstByte-Latency) and a roadmap ticket with runtime changes to gate prefetch concurrency by tenant and prefix. Target ETA for medium-term runtime gating: 2 weeks.
postmortem_followup: Create SDK advisory and publish recommended retry policy for streaming (assigned: Developer Experience team).
Implement runtime tenant+prefix prefetch coalescing to avoid duplicate prefetches across ephemeral workers (assigned: Runtime team).
Expose an accept-queue/backpressure metric to apigw for proactive rate limiting (assigned: Ingress team).
Add automated test in staging that simulates hedged-retry client against long-prefix workloads to catch regressions.
